topics.label: Course welcome and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final course lecture and outlines its core learning objectives concerning cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional cancer treatment modalities alongside the clinical challenges, including systemic toxicity and multidrug resistance, that restrict their success.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic approaches that selectively destroy tumor cells by taking advantage of their intrinsic functional and genetic vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the design of targeted therapies against oncogenic driver kinases and the diverse molecular mechanisms through which cancer cells develop resistance to them.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered antibodies are used to recognize tumor-associated cell-surface proteins to direct cytotoxicity or deliver lethal payloads.

topics.label: Cellular immunotherapy and immune checkpoint modulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between the immune system and cancer, detailing methods to harness and engineer host immune responses against tumors.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overarching evaluation of historical improvements in cancer outcomes, current systemic challenges, and future clinical considerations.
